answer: The lagoon of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. Work waits on the ripple until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the horizon of the next round. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on slash-on-divergence jury quorum, clawed back after a replayed submission, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
